correctness.rationale: For a,b,c>0 with a>b>=c, the min eigenvalue of Q restricted to n-perp lies in [a^-2,b^-2]; endpoint normals e1/e3 make essential R support [b,a]. With t=r^-2 and alpha=t-a^-2,beta=b^-2-t,gamma=c^-2-t>0, weighted Cauchy-Schwarz derives R<=r iff n1^2>=alpha(n2^2/beta+n3^2/gamma). Haar |n1| is uniform and transverse azimuth independent, yielding the displayed exact 2/pi integral, with strict CDF decrease in c and sharp c=b and c->0 envelopes. Dominated endpoint expansion gives elliptic E(k) coefficient L, strictly increasing in c. When a=b every plane intersects the top eigenspace, so R=a a.s. Independent direct 2x2 quadratic-form diagonalizations matched 80,000 cone event comparisons for 16,000 Haar normals, CDF quadrature and 400 a=b normals; these are finite corroborations, not the proof.

value.rationale: Determines the exact identifiability boundary of an intrinsically natural inverse stereology measurement: random unoriented central-plane largest section radius. Support gives a,b and any one interior CDF value fixes c, with sharp range and a precise multiplicity obstruction; a separate endpoint statistic provides redundancy. This is not merely restating the classical forward eigencompression density, and gives an exact benchmark for shape inference.
